reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Clerk powers to administer oaths and authenticate documents
headings.reviewNote: Covers authority of probate division clerk to take acknowledgments, administer oaths, authenticate documents and records, and perform office functions.

headings.title: Issuance of hearing notices and necessary orders
headings.reviewNote: Covers clerk authority, subject to judge control, to issue notices and enter orders for hearings on petitions or other matters.

headings.title: Determination of uncontested matters and thirty-day judge review
headings.reviewNote: Covers clerk determination of uncontested matters and orders or decrees, subject to judge modification or vacation within thirty days.

headings.title: Judge acting as ex officio clerk
headings.reviewNote: Covers authority of probate division judge to act as clerk ex officio when court business requires.

headings.title: Probate division seal custody
headings.reviewNote: Covers authorization of seal for circuit court probate division and custody by judge or clerk.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all five subsections on probate division clerk powers, hearing notices/orders, uncontested determinations with 30-day judicial review, judge acting ex officio, and seal custody (Effective 1-02-79).

headings.title: Document signing, oath or affirmation, and truth statement
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement that documents filed under probate code be signed and include statement under oath or affirmation subject to penalties for false declarations.

headings.title: Postjudgment validity despite form or substance defects
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule that defects of form or substance in documents do not invalidate proceedings after judgment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections on required signing and oath/affirmation statement for filed probate documents and postjudgment validity despite defects of form or substance (Effective 1-01-81).

headings.title: Notice requirements governed by code or court order
headings.reviewNote: Covers notice requirements to interested persons limited to specific code provisions or court rules and orders.

headings.title: Permissible methods and procedures for service of notice
headings.reviewNote: Covers service methods including personal delivery, newspaper publication under chapter 493 (see 1962 case annotation on weekly publication suspension), registered/certified mail, ordinary mail, or civil rules.

headings.title: Scope and binding effect of service by publication
headings.reviewNote: Covers effect of published service as notice to known or unknown heirs, devisees, spouses, creditors, and other interested persons.

headings.title: Exemption of creditors from nonpublication notice absent requirement
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule that nonpublication notices to interested persons do not include creditors unless specifically required by code or court order.

headings.title: Service upon minors, incapacitated persons, and corporations
headings.reviewNote: Covers service upon guardians or conservators of minors or disabled persons and service upon corporations in civil action manner.

headings.title: Ordinary mail service and validity despite nondelivery
headings.reviewNote: Covers ordinary mail service to persons in court files when publication is required, and rule that failure of receipt does not invalidate orders or jurisdiction.

headings.title: Persons authorized to make service and clerk duties
headings.reviewNote: Covers service by competent witnesses, sheriffs, or clerks upon written request with necessary information.

headings.title: Service upon attorney of record in lieu of party
headings.reviewNote: Covers service on attorney who entered written appearance, in lieu of party, by mail or delivery to office.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all eight subsections on probate notice requirements, service methods, publication scope, creditor exception, service on minors/corporations/attorneys, and clerk duties; notes 1962 case annotation on weekly newspaper publication.

headings.title: Requirement of record in adversary probate proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Covers mandatory stenographic or electronic recording in adversary probate proceedings under supreme court rules.

headings.title: Adversary probate proceeding defined
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory definition of adversary probate proceedings under chapters 472 to 475, exceptions absent objections, and judicial designations.

headings.title: Discretionary recording, security for costs, and assessment
headings.reviewNote: Covers judicial discretion to direct recording of hearings on motion or request, require security, and assess costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all three subsections on mandatory records in adversary probate proceedings, statutory definition with exceptions absent objections, and discretionary recording with cost security/assessment.

headings.title: Application of civil code and rules to adversary proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Covers governance of adversary probate proceedings by civil code and rules, subject to specific probate statutes and order requirement for chapter 509 and rule 55.

headings.title: Order designating pleading rules after commencement
headings.reviewNote: Covers court authority upon finding proceeding is adversary to enter order specifying applicable provisions of chapter 509 or civil rule 55.

headings.title: Civil rules governing other proceedings before probate judge
headings.reviewNote: Covers governance of other actions or proceedings heard by probate division judge by civil code and rules except as provided by law.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all three subsections on civil code and rules governing adversary probate proceedings, chapter 509 / civil rule 55 designation orders, and other proceedings heard by a probate division judge.

headings.title: Appealable orders, judgments, and decrees in probate division
headings.reviewNote: Covers appeal rights for aggrieved interested persons across fourteen enumerated probate categories, excluding orders admitting/rejecting wills; source includes seven 1966-1992 case annotations.

headings.title: Prerequisite motion to vacate clerk orders before appeal
headings.reviewNote: Covers prohibition of appeal from clerk orders absent court denial of motion to modify or vacate, and direct appealability of judge orders.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections on fourteen appealable probate categories and the prerequisite motion to modify/vacate clerk orders; notes seven 1966-1992 case annotations on aggrieved-party status and appealability.

headings.title: Appeals regarding mental condition and supersedeas conditions
headings.reviewNote: Covers appeals regarding mental condition and adjudication, limitation on automatic supersedeas, and standards for commitment or confinement stays.

headings.title: Guardian ad litem appointment upon denied supersedeas and review
headings.reviewNote: Covers appointment and disbursement authority of guardian ad litem upon denial of supersedeas and appellate review on motion.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections on appeals from mental-condition adjudications, supersedeas conditions, guardian ad litem appointment upon denied supersedeas, and appellate review on motion.

headings.title: Mandatory record books, indices, and registers
headings.reviewNote: Covers required records kept by probate division including decedent and protectee indices, chronological registers, abstracts, wills, bonds, letters, and minutes.

headings.title: Destruction of vouchers and receipts after five years
headings.reviewNote: Covers court authority to order destruction of vouchers and receipts on file for five years following final termination of administration.

headings.title: Non-bound record media, public reading equipment, and indexing
headings.reviewNote: Covers keeping probate records via photographic, electronic, or machine-readable media with publicly available reading equipment and adequate indexing.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all three subsections on ten mandatory probate division records, destruction of vouchers/receipts five years after final termination, and non-bound record media with public reading equipment and indexing.

headings.title: Scope and application to fiduciaries, agents, and trusts
headings.reviewNote: Covers applicability of sections 472.400 to 472.490 to fiduciaries, agents, personal representatives, conservatorships, and trustees whenever executed or commenced.

headings.title: Application to custodians based on user Missouri residency
headings.reviewNote: Covers application of digital asset statutes to custodians when the user is or was a Missouri resident at death.

headings.title: Exclusion of employer digital assets used in ordinary business
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory exclusion of employer digital assets used by employees in ordinary course of business.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all three subsections on digital asset act applicability to fiduciaries/agents/trustees/conservatorships, Missouri-resident custodians, and employer digital asset exclusion (L. 2018 H.B. 1250).

headings.title: Online tool directions regarding disclosure of digital assets
headings.reviewNote: Covers user authority to use online tool directing disclosure of digital assets and supremacy over contrary directions in wills, trusts, or powers of attorney.

headings.title: Directions in will, trust, or record absent online tool
headings.reviewNote: Covers user authority to allow or prohibit disclosure of digital assets in will, trust, power of attorney, or other record absent online tool direction.

headings.title: User directions overriding terms-of-service agreements
headings.reviewNote: Covers user direction overriding contrary terms-of-service provisions not requiring distinct affirmative user assent.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all three subsections on online tool directions, directions in wills/trusts/powers of attorney absent an online tool, and override of non-affirmative terms-of-service provisions (L. 2018 H.B. 1250).

headings.title: Terms-of-service agreement rights preserved
headings.reviewNote: Covers preservation of custodian and user rights under terms-of-service agreements to access and use digital assets.

headings.title: No expanded rights for fiduciaries or designated recipients
headings.reviewNote: Covers limitation that sections 472.400 to 472.490 confer no new or expanded rights on fiduciaries or designated recipients beyond those held by the user.

headings.title: Modification of access by user, federal law, or agreement
headings.reviewNote: Covers modification or elimination of fiduciary access by user, federal law, or terms-of-service agreement absent user directions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all three subsections preserving terms-of-service rights, barring new/expanded rights for fiduciaries or designated recipients, and allowing access modification by user, federal law, or agreement.

headings.title: Custodian options for granting access or copies
headings.reviewNote: Covers custodian discretion to grant full access, partial access, or copies in a record of accessible digital assets.

headings.title: Reasonable administrative charge for disclosure costs
headings.reviewNote: Covers custodian authorization to assess reasonable administrative charges for disclosing digital assets.

headings.title: Prohibition on disclosure of deleted digital assets
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory prohibition preventing custodians from disclosing digital assets deleted by the user.

headings.title: Undue burden exception to partial disclosure and court orders
headings.reviewNote: Covers custodian relief from segregation of assets imposing undue burden and authorization to seek court orders on disclosure scope.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all four subsections on custodian disclosure options, reasonable administrative charges, prohibition on disclosing deleted assets, and undue-burden partial-disclosure court orders.

headings.title: Court order granting conservator access after hearing
headings.reviewNote: Covers court authority to grant a conservator access to digital assets of a protected person after opportunity for hearing.

headings.title: Mandatory disclosure of communication catalogues and other assets
headings.reviewNote: Covers custodian duty to disclose catalogue of communications and non-content digital assets upon written request, court order, and account identifiers.

headings.title: Conservator request to suspend or terminate account for cause
headings.reviewNote: Covers conservator authority with general management powers to request account suspension or termination for good cause accompanied by court order.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all three subsections on court-ordered conservator access after hearing, mandatory custodian disclosure of communication catalogues and non-content assets, and account suspension/termination requests for good cause.

headings.title: Applicability of fiduciary duties to digital asset management
headings.reviewNote: Covers application of traditional fiduciary duties of care, loyalty, and confidentiality to managing digital assets.

headings.title: Scope of authority and prohibition on impersonation
headings.reviewNote: Covers limits on a fiduciary's or designated recipient's authority under terms of service, applicable law, duty scope, and prohibition on impersonating the user.

headings.title: Fiduciary right to access digital assets not held by custodian
headings.reviewNote: Covers fiduciary right to access decedent, protected person, principal, or settlor digital assets not held by custodian or subject to terms of service.

headings.title: Fiduciary authorized user status under computer fraud laws
headings.reviewNote: Covers authorized user status of fiduciary acting within duty scope for purposes of computer-fraud and unauthorized-access laws.

headings.title: Access to tangible personal property and stored digital assets
headings.reviewNote: Covers fiduciary right to access tangible personal property and stored digital assets as authorized user under computer laws.

headings.title: Custodian disclosure of information required for account termination
headings.reviewNote: Covers custodian authorization to disclose account information required to terminate an account used to access licensed digital assets.

headings.title: Written request procedure and documentation for account termination
headings.reviewNote: Covers written request requirements, death certificate, letters of authority or orders, and optional identifying data for account termination.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all seven subsections on fiduciary duties over digital assets, authority limits and impersonation bar, non-custodian and tangible-property access, computer-fraud authorized user status, and account termination procedures.

headings.title: Sixty-day deadline for custodian compliance and court orders
headings.reviewNote: Covers sixty-day custodian compliance deadline following required disclosures and court order application upon noncompliance.

headings.title: Required compliance finding under 18 U.S.C. Section 2702
headings.reviewNote: Covers required court finding that compliance order does not violate federal law under 18 U.S.C. Section 2702.

headings.title: Custodian discretion to notify user of request
headings.reviewNote: Covers custodian authorization to notify user that request for disclosure or account termination was submitted.

headings.title: Denial of request upon awareness of lawful post-request access
headings.reviewNote: Covers custodian discretion to deny disclosure or termination request upon awareness of lawful account access following request.

headings.title: Custodian ability to require court order
headings.reviewNote: Covers custodian ability to obtain or require a court order specifying account ownership, sufficient consent, and other legally required findings.

headings.title: Immunity for good-faith compliance
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory immunity from liability for custodians, officers, employees, and agents acting in good faith under digital asset statutes.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all six subsections on 60-day compliance deadline, 18 U.S.C. 2702 finding, user notification, denial upon lawful post-request access, custodian court-order requests, and good-faith immunity.
